46: /*
47:  * Coexistence netif wire id (2-bit co_hdr.vif_idx). Roles are NOT pinned to a
48:  * fixed LMAC VIF index any more (P2P GO/GC float on vif0/vif1 so the MCC
49:  * channel scheduler can handle them). We therefore key the wire id off the
50:  * (netif type, p2p) role instead of the LMAC index:
51:  *
52:  *   wire 0 = infra STA   (STA-type, !p2p) -> host g_mlan
53:  *   wire 1 = SoftAP      (AP-type,  !p2p) -> host g_uap
54:  *   wire 2 = P2P GO      (AP-type,   p2p) -> host g_p2p_go
55:  *   wire 3 = P2P GC      (STA-type,  p2p) -> host g_p2p_gc
56:  *
57:  * The TX path is symmetric: host tags the wire id, CP maps it back to the
58:  * current LMAC VIF index via cif_wire_to_lmac_vif() (no longer identity).
59:  */
60: static uint8_t cif_vif_to_netif_wire(void *vif)
61: {
62:     netif_if_t t = wifi_netif_vif_to_netif_type(vif);
63:     bool p2p = cif_vif_is_p2p(vif);
64: 
65:     if ((t == NETIF_IF_AP) && p2p)
66:         return 2;
67:     if ((t == NETIF_IF_STA) && p2p)
68:         return 3;
69: 
70:     return (uint8_t)t;
71: }
72: 
73: /*
74:  * Reverse of cif_vif_to_netif_wire(): map a host wire id back to the LMAC VIF
75:  * index currently held by that role. Since GO/GC float on vif0/vif1, the old
76:  * identity mapping (wire==index) no longer holds, so look the role up in the
77:  * active VIF table. Falls back to the wire id if no active match is found.
78:  */
79: static uint8_t cif_wire_to_lmac_vif(uint8_t wire)
80: {
81:     netif_if_t want_type;
82:     bool want_p2p;
83: 
84:     switch (wire)
85:     {
86:         case 0: want_type = NETIF_IF_STA; want_p2p = false; break;
87:         case 1: want_type = NETIF_IF_AP;  want_p2p = false; break;
88:         case 2: want_type = NETIF_IF_AP;  want_p2p = true;  break;
89:         case 3: want_type = NETIF_IF_STA; want_p2p = true;  break;
90:         default: return wire;
91:     }
92: 
93:     for (void *vif = mac_vif_mgmt_first_vif(); vif != NULL;
94:          vif = mac_vif_mgmt_next_vif(vif))
95:     {
96:         if ((wifi_netif_vif_to_netif_type(vif) == want_type) &&
97:             (cif_vif_is_p2p(vif) == want_p2p))
98:             return wifi_netif_vif_to_vifid(vif);
99:     }
100: 
101:     return wire;
102: }

**Findings**
1. **Critical: AP-side IPv4 never starts DHCP and may reuse a stale lease.**  
[notify.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/wpa_supplicant-2.10/wpa_supplicant/notify.c:381) now sends `CIF_WIFI_EVT_STA_CONNECTED` immediately after association, before either core has an IPv4 address. AP receives it in [wdrv_cntrl.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_wifi_driver/wdrv_cntrl.c:545), but does not clear the old `connect_ind.ip/mk/gw/dns`. Then [bk_netif.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_netif/bk_netif.c:91) calls `sta_ip_mode_set(0)` and installs those fields as a static address. On the first connection they are `0.0.0.0`; after reconnect they can contain the previous lease. No DHCP request is generated, so forwarding ARP and IPv4 to AP does not produce a usable AP-owned IPv4 stack.

Exact fix: define/mirror `WIFI_VNET_AP_IPV4` in [AP Wi-Fi-driver Kconfig](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_wifi_driver/Kconfig:2), enable it in the AP project config, and change [bk_netif.c:91](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_netif/bk_netif.c:91) to use DHCP in this mode:

```c
#if CONFIG_WIFI_VNET_AP_IPV4
        sta_ip_down();
        sta_ip_mode_set(1);
        sta_ip_start();
#else
        /* existing CP-provided static-IP handoff */
#endif
```

Also clear `connect_ind.ip`, `mk`, `gw`, and `dns` at [wdrv_cntrl.c:545](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_wifi_driver/wdrv_cntrl.c:545) when handling the early link event.

2. **High: the ownership switch applies to SoftAP as well as infrastructure STA.**  
The Kconfig help at [Kconfig:13](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/controller_if/Kconfig:13) says “STA ARP and IPv4,” but [cif_wifi_dp.c:470](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/controller_if/cif_wifi_dp.c:470) and [cif_wifi_dp.c:559](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/controller_if/cif_wifi_dp.c:559) test only the global symbol. With `P2P=n`, this still affects both wire 0/STA and wire 1/SoftAP. Consequently SoftAP DHCP-server, DNS, local-port, ICMP-echo and other IPv4 packets that the old filter retained on CP are transferred exclusively to AP. The CP config has hostapd enabled at [config:407](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app_ab/cp/config/bk7258/config:407), so this is reachable.

Exact fix: compute a per-packet role predicate near [cif_wifi_dp.c:443](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/controller_if/cif_wifi_dp.c:443):

```c
bool ap_owns_ipv4 = false;
#if CONFIG_WIFI_VNET_AP_IPV4
ap_owns_ipv4 = wifi_netif_vif_to_netif_type(vif) == NETIF_IF_STA &&
               !cif_vif_is_p2p(vif);
#endif
```

Use `ap_owns_ipv4` for the zero-copy ARP branch, and replace the preprocessor-generated `if (true)` with:

```c
if (ap_owns_ipv4 || cif_filter_check_ip_data(p) == false)
```

This preserves CP ownership/filtering for SoftAP and P2P roles.

3. **Medium: one outage can generate two AP disconnect events.**  
[notify.c:449](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/wpa_supplicant-2.10/wpa_supplicant/notify.c:449) sends the AP event before the auto-reconnect suppression at lines 466-469. If reconnection subsequently exhausts its scans, [wpa_scan.c:2906](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/wpa_supplicant-2.10/wpa_supplicant/wpa_scan.c:2906) sends another `CIF_WIFI_EVT_STA_DISCONNECTED`. AP therefore executes `sta_ip_down()` and posts the application event twice for one link loss.

The old block at [notify.c:473](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/wpa_supplicant-2.10/wpa_supplicant/notify.c:473) correctly excludes AP-IPv4 mode, so there is no immediate double-send within `wpas_notify_disconnected()` itself.

Exact fix: if immediate AP teardown is required, keep the new event and change [wpa_scan.c:2906](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/wpa_supplicant-2.10/wpa_supplicant/wpa_scan.c:2906) to:

```c
#if CONFIG_WIFI_VNET_CONTROLLER && !CONFIG_WIFI_VNET_AP_IPV4
```

Alternatively, move lines 449-464 inside the existing reconnect-notification block, accepting delayed AP teardown.

4. **Medium: direct-push completion can leak the original CP RX pbuf.**  
The new ARP path and all-IPv4 path make the existing direct-push completion mechanism the normal path for nearly every STA frame. AP copies the frame, marks the shared CP pbuf `need_free`, and returns it at [wdrv_rx.c:132](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_wifi_driver/wdrv_rx.c:132). If `wdrv_txdata_sender()` fails at line 134, it only undoes the temporary reference at [wdrv_tx.c:107](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_wifi_driver/wdrv_tx.c:107); CP never receives the completion and the original RX pbuf remains permanently owned.

Exact fix: treat `need_free` completion messages as non-droppable. Retry or place them on a guaranteed completion queue when [wdrv_rx.c:134](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_wifi_driver/wdrv_rx.c:134) fails. Logging and continuing is insufficient.

The normal successful path is balanced, but [cif_wifi_dp.c:175](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/controller_if/cif_wifi_dp.c:175) directly decrements `pbuf->ref` outside lwIP protection. Replace the manual decrement plus one free with two `pbuf_free(pbuf)` calls, or add a proper ownership-release helper. This preserves the two intended dereferences while using lwIP’s protected refcount API.

5. **Low: the project override config was replaced by generated output.**  
[app_ab CP config](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app_ab/cp/config/bk7258/config:1) changed from three maintained overrides to 1,097 lines of “Automatically generated, DO NOT EDIT” state. This captures unrelated defaults and makes future Kconfig changes ineffective or unexpectedly sticky.

Exact fix: restore the concise override file and add only:

```text
CONFIG_WIFI_VNET_AP_IPV4=y
```

Keep the existing three GPIO overrides. `WIFI_VNET_CONTROLLER` and `CONTROLLER_RX_DIRECT_PSH` must remain enabled by the inherited project configuration because they are dependencies of [Kconfig:10](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/controller_if/Kconfig:10).

**Compile And Preprocessor**
No compile failure was found in the three changed CP translation units. I replayed their ARM compile commands with `CONFIG_WIFI_VNET_AP_IPV4=1`, `CONFIG_P2P` undefined, and the existing `-Wall -Werror` flags; `cif_wifi_dp.c`, `net.c`, and `notify.c` all compiled cleanly. The nested P2P `if/else` preprocessing in `notify.c` is syntactically valid for P2P on/off and AP-IPv4 on/off.

A complete `make bk7258` could not run because `cmake` is absent from `PATH`; it stopped before source compilation. The existing generated `sdkconfig.h` is stale and does not contain `CONFIG_WIFI_VNET_AP_IPV4`, so prior build artifacts do not validate this change.

**Forwarding Verdict**
For infrastructure STA packet selection alone, ARP and every Ethernet IPv4 frame are transferred to AP, while EAPOL remains on CP. The direct-push ownership is balanced on successful completion.

End-to-end behavior is **not correct** with `CONFIG_WIFI_VNET_AP_IPV4=y` and `P2P=n`: AP currently configures static `0.0.0.0` or a stale lease instead of DHCP, and the global checks also steal SoftAP IPv4/ARP traffic from CP.
